findings.title: Server auth repository bypasses the declared HTTP/MSW boundary
evidence: src/features/auth/infrastructure/http/http-auth.repository.ts already implements the AuthRepository contract over /api/v1/auth/sessions
src/instrumentation.ts starts the MSW Node server and the architecture rule declares it authoritative
findings.decision: Next bite must align server auth repository resolution with the declared infrastructure boundary without changing authentication behavior.
resolution: server runtime code is forbidden from importing auth.mock-store directly by the Wave 02 gate
src/features/auth/server/auth-server.repository.test.ts proves the server factory composes the canonical HTTP adapter/origin while existing Auth handler tests prove the adapter over MSW Node

findings.title: Protected-route ownership is leaf-feature based rather than route-boundary based
evidence: CanvasPage protects /canvas while loading the authenticated project
findings.decision: Do not move protection yet. First preserve the two existing contracts with an executable gate; evaluate route-layout ownership in a dedicated wave.
resolution: src/app/canvas/page.tsx now owns requireAuthenticatedSession('/canvas') before entering the Canvas feature
src/app/canvas/resultado/page.tsx now owns requireAuthenticatedSession('/canvas/resultado') and preserves its exact returnTo contract
Canvas feature pages now receive AuthUser explicitly and the project loader accepts ownerId instead of owning route authentication
Wave 03 gate forbids route protection from drifting back into Canvas feature loaders

findings.title: returnTo sanitization permits the login route itself
evidence: AuthPage redirects an already authenticated user to the sanitized returnTo
findings.decision: Add explicit redirect-policy tests before changing sanitizer behavior.
resolution: sanitizeReturnTo preserves local single-slash return targets but rejects the /login route itself, including query/hash variants, back to AUTH_DEFAULT_RETURN_TO
src/features/auth/server/auth-session.test.ts freezes accepted and rejected redirect targets
Wave 04 gate requires AuthPage, loginAction and requireAuthenticatedSession to continue consuming the canonical sanitizer instead of growing independent redirect policy

findings.title: Cross-feature auth consumption is not consistently facade-based
evidence: Canvas UI imports AuthUser from auth/domain in multiple files
Canvas UI imports UserMenu from auth/ui/user-menu directly
Other Canvas files already consume AuthUser through @/features/auth
findings.decision: Defer broad cross-feature boundary cleanup; SO-019 owns application-wide boundary governance unless SO-016 needs a smaller auth-specific facade bite.
resolution: src/features/auth/index.ts exports AuthUser and UserMenu as the approved client-safe cross-feature facade surface
Canvas UI imports AuthUser/UserMenu only through @/features/auth; direct auth domain/ui/application/infrastructure/server imports are forbidden there by the Wave 05 gate
Canvas server actions keep explicit @/features/auth/server/auth-session imports so server-only session code is not leaked through the client-safe facade

findings.title: Existing auth gate does not fully prove protected-route coverage
evidence: check-auth-msw.mjs checks that auth-session contains a server redirect
it does not assert that both /canvas and /canvas/resultado resolve through requireAuthenticatedSession with their own returnTo values
findings.decision: Wave 01 introduces an audit gate that freezes current protected-route coverage before runtime refactors.
resolution: Wave 03 executable gate proves /canvas and /canvas/resultado route entries call requireAuthenticatedSession with exact returnTo values
Canvas feature loaders are forbidden from regaining route-auth ownership

nextBite.title: Application Shell & Shared UI Armor
nextBite.reason: SO-016 is complete; continue the application-wide armor sequence with an audit-first SO-017.

closeout.verdict: No additional auth/protected-surface runtime bite is proven necessary. SO-016 may close without broad refactor.
